title: PR test pipeline on the self-hosted runner: the PR-reviewer hands the build and tests to GitHub Actions when a runner is online

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "there should be an agent change and prob pr-reviewer change that when the pr-review is done instead of doing the build locally, we check if there is hosted github runners present and push the testing as PR build to the github actions self hosted runner... Which means prob both the pr-reviewer skill need or just the skill need to be able to determine that and the testing pipeline needs to be created."

Related: issue 1413 (cut pipeline, Linux, self-hosted runners only), issue 1415 / PR 1416 (removes the unused `ci.yml` and `nightly.yml`).

## Why

Every PR review builds the workspace and runs the touched suites in a worktree on the reviewer's machine: 10-20 GB of `target/` each, up to four at once, competing with gates and cuts for the same machine.

## What

1. **A PR test workflow** (here `pr-test.yml`) for the self-hosted Linux runner (`runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`): input is a PR number; it trial-merges the PR head with current main, builds, runs `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (the suites the diff touches) and clippy for the touched crates, and reports pass/fail per binary with the failing output.
2. **Runner detection.** Before building, the reviewer asks whether a self-hosted runner is online (`gh api repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runners --jq '.runners[] | select(.status=="online")'`). Online: start the workflow for the PR (`gh workflow run pr-test.yml -f pr=<N>`), wait for the run (`gh run watch`), and read its result and logs into the review. None online, or the run cannot start: build locally as today. The review comment says which of the two ran, with the run's link.
3. **Where the logic lives.** In the `review-prs` skill and the `PR-reviewer` agent definition (`.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`); decide whether detection sits in the skill (the dispatcher starts the run, the reviewer reads it) or in the agent. The reviewer still reads the diff, checks AGENTS.md's laws and writes the review itself; only the build and test step moves.

## Open questions (decide before code)

- **Trigger and safety.** A self-hosted runner executes the PR's code (build scripts, tests) on the maintainer's hardware. AGENTS.md says "Never add a `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger without the user's say-so". Proposed: `workflow_dispatch` only, started by a collaborator's session, so a fork PR can never start a run by itself; the job gets no secrets and a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the runner works in a clean checkout per run. A `pull_request` trigger for PRs from collaborators' own branches is the alternative, and needs the maintainer's explicit yes.
- **`needs-maintainer` PRs.** Today a PR with a new dependency or a `build.rs` / scripts / `.github` change is read, not built. That rule should hold on the runner too.
- **Linux only.** Windows-only readings (per-OS pinned values, the Windows arm of issue 1402) are not checked by a Linux run; say whether the reviewer still runs those locally when the diff touches them.
- **Concurrency.** One runner, up to four reviews: a queue (`concurrency:` per PR), and what the reviewer does while it waits.
- **UI tests.** The ui suites spawn the real app through the test harness; say whether the runner can run them headless or they stay local.
- **Fallback truthfulness.** A run that is cancelled or times out is not a pass: the reviewer falls back to the local build or reports "not built".

## Also changes

`.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`, `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md` and AGENTS.md ("Outside PRs are reviewed", "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted") are process files: the PR bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and is announced on issue 681. A `.github` change is read by the maintainer before it merges.

Done means: with the runner online, a review of a test PR starts the workflow, the review comment carries the run's link and per-binary result, and no local build ran; with the runner offline, the same review builds locally as today; a fork PR cannot start the workflow by itself; AGENTS.md and the runner setup notes describe it.
